rule_name: Worker must be a natural person, male or female, who works for an employer and under the employer's management or supervision in return for a wage

original_text: Non-Saudi workers who enter the Kingdom to perform a specific task for a period not exceeding two months.

rule_name: Employer must prepare work organization regulations
description: Every employer shall prepare work organization regulations for the establishment in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry. The Minister may grant an exemption from this requirement.
original_text: Every employer shall prepare work organization regulations for the establishment in accordance with the form prepared by the Ministry. The Minister may grant an exemption from this requirement.

rule_name: Employer may include additional terms and provisions
description: The employer may include additional terms and provisions in such regulations, provided they do not conflict with this Law, its Implementing Regulations, or decisions issued for its implementation.
original_text: The employer may include additional terms and provisions in such regulations, provided they do not conflict with this Law, its Implementing Regulations, or decisions issued for its implementation.

rule_name: Employer must announce work organization regulations
description: The employer shall announce the work organization regulations and any amendments thereto in a conspicuous place in the establishment or by any other means that ensures that persons subject to the regulations are aware of their provisions.
original_text: The employer shall announce the work organization regulations and any amendments thereto in a conspicuous place in the establishment or by any other means that ensures that persons subject to the regulations are aware of their provisions.

description: The predecessor and successor may agree, with the worker's written consent, that all pre-existing rights of the worker shall transfer to the new owner. If the worker does not consent, the worker may request termination of the contract and receive the worker's entitlements from the predecessor.
original_text: reason, the predecessor and successor may agree, with the worker's written consent, that all pre-existing rights of the worker shall transfer to the new owner. If the worker does not consent, the worker may request termination of the contract and receive the worker's entitlements from the predecessor.

description: Amounts due to a worker or the worker's heirs under this Law shall constitute first-ranking privileged debts. For the purpose of recovering such amounts, the worker and the worker's heirs shall have a privilege over all assets of the employer.
original_text: Amounts due to a worker or the worker's heirs under this Law shall constitute first-ranking privileged debts. For the purpose of recovering such amounts, the worker and the worker's heirs shall have a privilege over all assets of the employer.

description: In the event of the employer's bankruptcy or liquidation of the establishment, such amounts shall be registered as privileged debts, and the worker shall be paid, on an expedited basis, an amount equivalent to one month's wage before payment of any other expenses, including court costs and bankruptcy or liquidation expenses.
original_text: In the event of the employer's bankruptcy or liquidation of the establishment, such amounts shall be registered as privileged debts, and the worker shall be paid, on an expedited basis, an amount equivalent to one month's wage before payment of any other expenses, including court costs and bankruptcy or liquidation expenses.

description: Neither the employer nor the worker may undertake any act that constitutes an abuse of the provisions of this Law or of the decisions and regulations issued for its implementation. Neither party may undertake any act intended to exert pressure on the freedom of the other party, or on the freedom of other workers or employers, for the purpose of achieving any interest or viewpoint in a manner inconsistent with freedom of work or with the jurisdiction of the competent authority for settlement of disputes.
original_text: Neither the employer nor the worker may undertake any act that constitutes an abuse of the provisions of this Law or of the decisions and regulations issued for its implementation. Neither party may undertake any act intended to exert pressure on the freedom of the other party, or on the freedom of other workers or employers, for the purpose of achieving any interest or viewpoint in a manner inconsistent with freedom of work or with the jurisdiction of the competent authority for settlement of disputes.

description: Every citizen who is of working age, able to work, and willing to work may request registration through the recruitment channels, stating the citizen's date of birth, qualifications, previous work experience, preferences, and address.
applicability: Every citizen who is of working age, able to work, and willing to work
original_text: Every citizen who is of working age, able to work, and willing to work may request registration through the recruitment channels, stating the citizen's date of birth, qualifications, previous work experience, preferences, and address.

description: Every employer shall submit the following to the Ministry: a statement of vacant and newly created positions, a notice of the action taken regarding the employment of a citizen nominated through the recruitment channels, a statement containing the names of the employer's workers, their positions, occupations, wages, ages, nationalities, the numbers and dates of work permits for non-Saudi workers, and any other information specified by the Implementing Regulations.
original_text: Every employer shall submit the following to the Ministry: a statement of vacant and newly created positions, a notice of the action taken regarding the employment of a citizen nominated through the recruitment channels, a statement containing the names of the employer's workers, their positions, occupations, wages, ages, nationalities, the numbers and dates of work permits for non-Saudi workers, and any other information specified by the Implementing Regulations.

description: All establishments shall endeavor to attract and employ Saudi nationals, provide means to support their continued employment, and afford them an appropriate opportunity to demonstrate their suitability for work.
applicability: All establishments, regardless of their activities or the number of workers employed.
original_text: All establishments, regardless of their activities or the number of workers employed, shall endeavor to attract and employ Saudi nationals, provide means to support their continued employment, and afford them an appropriate opportunity to demonstrate their suitability for work through guidance, training, and qualification for the duties assigned to them.

description: The proportion of Saudi workers employed by an employer shall not be less than 75% of the employer's total workforce. Where the required technical competencies or academic qualifications are unavailable, or where positions cannot be filled by Saudi nationals, the Minister may temporarily reduce this percentage.
condition: Where the required technical competencies or academic qualifications are unavailable, or where positions cannot be filled by Saudi nationals.
original_text: The proportion of Saudi workers employed by an employer shall not be less than 75% of the employer's total workforce. Where the required technical competencies or academic qualifications are unavailable, or where positions cannot be filled by Saudi nationals, the Minister may temporarily reduce this percentage.

rule_name: Employment of Workers through Recruitment Channels
description: Where necessary, the Minister may require employers, in specified activities or occupations and in specified regions or governorates, not to employ workers unless such workers have first been registered through the recruitment channels, subject to the conditions and arrangements prescribed by a decision of the Minister.
applicability: Employers in specified activities or occupations and in specified regions or governorates.
original_text: Where necessary, the Minister may require employers, in specified activities or occupations and in specified regions or governorates, not to employ workers unless such workers have first been registered through the recruitment channels, subject to the conditions and arrangements prescribed by a decision of the Minister.

description: Every employer who employs twenty-five workers or more, and whose work is of a nature that enables the employment of professionally qualified persons with disabilities, shall ensure that professionally qualified persons with disabilities constitute at least 4% of the employer's total workforce, whether such persons are nominated through recruitment channels or otherwise.
applicability: Employers who employ twenty-five workers or more, and whose work is of a nature that enables the employment of professionally qualified persons with disabilities.
original_text: Every employer who employs twenty-five workers or more, and whose work is of a nature that enables the employment of professionally qualified persons with disabilities, shall ensure that professionally qualified persons with disabilities constitute at least 4% of the employer's total workforce, whether such persons are nominated through recruitment channels or otherwise.

rule_name: Employment of Workers with Work Injuries
description: If a worker suffers a work injury that results in a reduction in the worker's normal capabilities but does not prevent the worker from performing another type of work, the employer with whom the work injury occurred shall employ the worker in suitable work at the wage prescribed for that work. This shall not prejudice the worker's entitlement to compensation for the injury.
applicability: Employers with whom the work injury occurred.
original_text: If a worker suffers a work injury that results in a reduction in the worker's normal capabilities but does not prevent the worker from performing another type of work, the employer with whom the work injury occurred shall employ the worker in suitable work at the wage prescribed for that work. This shall not prejudice the worker's entitlement to compensation for the injury.

rule_name: Employment of Workers through Employment Offices or Companies
description: Saudi workers whose employment is facilitated by employment offices or companies, and workers recruited by recruitment offices or companies on behalf of employers, shall be considered workers of the relevant employer and shall have a direct contractual relationship with that employer.
applicability: Employers and workers facilitated by employment offices or companies, and workers recruited by recruitment offices or companies on behalf of employers.
original_text: Saudi workers whose employment is facilitated by employment offices or companies, and workers recruited by recruitment offices or companies on behalf of employers, shall be considered workers of the relevant employer and shall have a direct contractual relationship with that employer.

description: Recruitment for employment is not permitted without prior approval from the Ministry.
original_text: Recruitment for the purpose of employment shall not be permitted without the prior approval of the Ministry.

description: A non-Saudi person must obtain a work permit from the Ministry before engaging in any work.
original_text: A non-Saudi person may not engage in any work, nor may such person be permitted to do so, unless a work permit has first been obtained from the Ministry in the form prescribed for that purpose.

description: Conditions for issuance of the work permit include lawful entry into the Kingdom, authorization to work, professional competencies or academic qualifications, and contract with an employer.
original_text: The following conditions shall be satisfied for issuance of the permit: 1. The worker must have entered the Kingdom lawfully and be authorized to work. 2. The worker must possess professional competencies or academic qualifications needed in the Kingdom and not sufficiently available among Saudi nationals, or must belong to a category of ordinary workers needed in the Kingdom. 3. The worker must be under contract with an employer and under that employer's responsibility.

description: The Ministry may decline to renew a work permit if the employer violates employment-nationalization standards or other requirements.
original_text: For reasons it deems appropriate, the Ministry may decline to renew a work permit where the employer violates the employment-nationalization standards prescribed by the Ministry or any other requirements or controls set out in the Implementing Regulations.

description: The Ministry may determine occupations and types of work in which non-Saudis are prohibited from engaging.
original_text: The Minister shall, by decision, determine the occupations and types of work in which non-Saudis are prohibited from engaging.

description: The employment contract of a non-Saudi worker must be in writing and for a fixed term.
original_text: The employment contract of a non-Saudi worker shall be in writing and for a fixed term.

description: Employers may not allow workers to change occupations without completing prescribed legal procedures.
original_text: An employer may not employ a worker in an occupation other than the occupation specified in the worker's work permit. A worker may not work in an occupation other than the occupation stated in the permit before the prescribed legal procedures for changing the occupation have been completed.

description: Employers may not allow workers to work for another person or for their own account.
original_text: Except in accordance with the prescribed legal rules and procedures, an employer may not allow the employer's worker to work for another person or for the worker's own account. A worker may not work for another employer or for the worker's own account, and an employer may not employ another employer's worker.

description: The Ministry shall inspect establishments and take measures to apply penalties prescribed by this Law.
original_text: The Ministry shall inspect establishments, detect violations of this Law, and take the measures necessary to apply the penalties prescribed hereunder.

description: The employer shall bear the fees for recruitment of a non-Saudi worker; the fees for the residence permit and work permit and their renewal; any fines resulting from delay for which the employer is responsible; the fees for changing the occupation; exit and re-entry fees; and the cost of the worker's return ticket to the worker's home country upon termination of the relationship between the parties.
original_text: The employer shall bear the fees for recruitment of a non-Saudi worker; the fees for the residence permit and work permit and their renewal; any fines resulting from delay for which the employer is responsible; the fees for changing the occupation; exit and re-entry fees; and the cost of the worker's return ticket to the worker's home country upon termination of the relationship between the parties.

description: The worker shall bear the cost of returning to the worker's country if the worker is found unfit for work or wishes to return without a legitimate reason.
original_text: The worker shall bear the cost of returning to the worker's country if the worker is found unfit for work or wishes to return without a legitimate reason.

description: The employer to whom a worker wishes to transfer shall bear the fees for transferring the worker's services.
original_text: The employer to whom a worker wishes to transfer shall bear the fees for transferring the worker's services.

description: The employer shall be exempt from the obligation to prepare the body of a deceased worker and transport it to the place where the contract was concluded or from which the worker was recruited, unless the worker is buried in the Kingdom with the consent of the worker's family. The employer shall be exempt from this obligation where the General Organization for Social Insurance assumes such costs.
original_text: The employer shall be exempt from the obligation to prepare the body of a deceased worker and transport it to the place where the contract was concluded or from which the worker was recruited, unless the worker is buried in the Kingdom with the consent of the worker's family. The employer shall be exempt from this obligation where the General Organization for Social Insurance assumes such costs.

description: Every employer shall establish a policy for training and qualifying the employer's Saudi workers with the aim of developing their skills and improving their level of performance in technical, administrative, vocational, and other work.
original_text: Every employer shall establish a policy for training and qualifying the employer's Saudi workers with the aim of developing their skills and improving their level of performance in technical, administrative, vocational, and other work. The Implementing Regulations shall determine the provisions relating thereto.

description: Without prejudice to any special conditions or rules concerning training, qualification, and skill development contained in concession agreements or other agreements, every employer shall qualify or train a percentage of the employer's Saudi workers in the work carried out by the employer. Such percentage shall be determined by a decision of the Minister. Saudi workers who continue their studies shall be counted toward that percentage where the employer bears the cost of such studies.
original_text: Without prejudice to any special conditions or rules concerning training, qualification, and skill development contained in concession agreements or other agreements, every employer shall qualify or train a percentage of the employer's Saudi workers in the work carried out by the employer. Such percentage shall be determined by a decision of the Minister. Saudi workers who continue their studies shall be counted toward that percentage where the employer bears the cost of such studies.

description: A training program shall specify the skill in which the worker is to be trained; the rules and conditions governing the training; the duration and number of training hours; the theoretical and practical training programs; the examination method; and the certificates to be awarded.
original_text: A training program shall specify the skill in which the worker is to be trained; the rules and conditions governing the training; the duration and number of training hours; the theoretical and practical training programs; the examination method; and the certificates to be awarded.

description: A qualification and training contract is a contract under which an employer undertakes to qualify or train a person in preparation for a specified occupation.
original_text: A qualification and training contract is a contract under which an employer undertakes to qualify or train a person in preparation for a specified occupation.

description: A qualification or training contract shall be in writing and shall specify the occupation for which the person is to be trained, the duration and successive stages of the training, the skill intended to be acquired, and the amount of the allowance payable to the trainee at each stage, provided that such allowance is not determined on a piece-rate or production basis. The contract shall also specify the rights and duties of both the trainee and the employer, and whether the qualification or training will take place at an establishment belonging to the employer or at another establishment.
original_text: A qualification or training contract shall be in writing and shall specify the occupation for which the person is to be trained, the duration and successive stages of the training, the skill intended to be acquired, and the amount of the allowance payable to the trainee at each stage, provided that such allowance is not determined on a piece-rate or production basis. The contract shall also specify the rights and duties of both the trainee and the employer, and whether the qualification or training will take place at an establishment belonging to the employer or at another establishment.

description: The Minister may require establishments to accept a specified number or percentage of students and graduates of universities, colleges, institutes, and training centers for the purpose of training and completing practical experience, in accordance with the conditions, arrangements, and periods prescribed by the Implementing Regulations. A training contract shall be concluded between the trainee and the employer, and the provisions of this Chapter shall apply thereto. The establishment may pay the trainee an allowance.
original_text: The Minister may require establishments to accept a specified number or percentage of students and graduates of universities, colleges, institutes, and training centers for the purpose of training and completing practical experience, in accordance with the conditions, arrangements, and periods prescribed by the Implementing Regulations. A training contract shall be concluded between the trainee and the employer, and the provisions of this Chapter shall apply thereto. The establishment may pay the trainee an allowance.

description: An employer may terminate a qualification or training contract if it is established that the trainee or person undergoing qualification lacks the aptitude or ability to complete the training or qualification.
original_text: An employer may terminate a qualification or training contract if it is established that the trainee or person undergoing qualification lacks the aptitude or ability to complete the training or qualification.

description: A party wishing to terminate the contract shall notify the other party at least one week before the specified termination date.
original_text: A party wishing to terminate the contract shall notify the other party at least one week before the specified termination date.

description: Neither party may claim compensation from the other unless the contract contains a provision to that effect.
original_text: Neither party may claim compensation from the other unless the contract contains a provision to that effect.

rule_name: Training or Qualification Period Work Requirement
description: The employer may require the trainee or person undergoing qualification to work for the employer for a period equal to the period of training or qualification.
original_text: Upon completion of the training or qualification period, the employer may require the trainee or person undergoing qualification to work for the employer for a period equal to the period of training or qualification.

description: If the trainee or person undergoing qualification refuses or fails to work for all or part of that equivalent period, the trainee shall reimburse the employer for the training or qualification costs borne by the employer, in full or in proportion to the unserved portion of the required period.
original_text: If the trainee or person undergoing qualification refuses or fails to work for all or part of that equivalent period, the trainee shall reimburse the employer for the training or qualification costs borne by the employer, in full or in proportion to the unserved portion of the required period.

description: An employment contract is a contract concluded between an employer and a worker under which the worker undertakes to work under the management or supervision of the employer in return for a wage.
applicability: Employment contracts concluded between an employer and a worker.
original_text: An employment contract is a contract concluded between an employer and a worker under which the worker undertakes to work under the management or supervision of the employer in return for a wage.

description: The Ministry shall prepare a standard form for each type of employment contract, containing minimum information such as employer's name and place of business, worker's name and nationality, identity information, residential address, agreed wage, type and place of work, date of commencement, duration of the contract if fixed-term, and principal rights and obligations of each party.
applicability: Standard form for each type of employment contract.
original_text: 1. Subject to Article 37 of this Law, the Ministry shall prepare a standard form for each type of employment contract. The form shall contain, as a minimum, the employer's name and place of business; the worker's name and nationality; information required to establish the worker's identity; the worker's residential address; the agreed wage, including benefits and allowances; the type and place of work; the date of commencement; the duration of the contract if fixed-term; and the principal rights and obligations of each party.

description: If the worker is to be subject to a probationary period, this shall be expressly stated in the employment contract and its duration shall be clearly specified. In all cases, the total probationary period shall not exceed one hundred and eighty days.
original_text: If the worker is to be subject to a probationary period, this shall be expressly stated in the employment contract and its duration shall be clearly specified. In all cases, the total probationary period shall not exceed one hundred and eighty days.

description: The total probationary period shall not exceed one hundred and eighty days.
original_text: The total probationary period shall not exceed one hundred and eighty days.

description: The Implementing Regulations shall set out the related provisions, including leave that is excluded from the calculation of the probationary period.
original_text: The Implementing Regulations shall set out the related provisions, including leave that is excluded from the calculation of the probationary period.

description: Either party may terminate the contract during this period.
original_text: Either party may terminate the contract during this period.

description: If the contract is terminated during the probationary period, neither party shall be entitled to compensation and the worker shall not be entitled to an end-of-service award in respect of that period.
original_text: If the contract is terminated during the probationary period, neither party shall be entitled to compensation and the worker shall not be entitled to an end-of-service award in respect of that period.

rule_name: Entitlement to wage for non-working period
description: If a worker reports for work at the prescribed time or establishes readiness to work at that time and is prevented from working for a reason attributable to the employer, the worker shall be entitled to the wage for the period during which no work is performed.
original_text: If a worker reports for work at the prescribed time, or establishes readiness to work at that time, and is prevented from working for a reason attributable to the employer, the worker shall be entitled to the wage for the period during which no work is performed.

rule_name: Prohibition of prohibited substances in workplaces
description: The employer, the employer's representative, and any person having authority over workers shall prevent the introduction into workplaces of any substance prohibited under Islamic Sharia. Any person found in possession of or using such substance shall be subject to the penalties prescribed by this Law, without prejudice to penalties prescribed under Sharia.
original_text: The employer, the employer's representative, and any person having authority over workers shall prevent the introduction into workplaces of any substance prohibited under Islamic Sharia. Any person found in possession of or using such substance shall be subject to the penalties prescribed by this Law, without prejudice to penalties prescribed under Sharia.

description: Upon termination of the employment contract, the employer shall provide the worker free of charge with a certificate of service stating the date on which employment commenced, the date on which the relationship ended, the worker's occupation, and the amount of the worker's final wage. The employer may not include in the certificate anything that could damage the worker's reputation or reduce the worker's employment opportunities.
original_text:
Upon termination of the employment contract, the employer shall:
1. At the worker's request, provide the worker free of charge with a certificate of service stating the date on which employment commenced, the date on which the relationship ended, the worker's occupation, and the amount of the worker's final wage. The employer may not include in the certificate anything that could damage the worker's reputation or reduce the worker's employment opportunities.

description: Upon termination of the employment contract, the employer shall return to the worker all certificates and documents deposited with the employer.
original_text:
Upon termination of the employment contract, the employer shall:
2. Return to the worker all certificates and documents deposited with the employer.

description:
In addition to the duties prescribed by this Law and by the regulations and decisions issued for its implementation, a worker shall:
1. Perform the work in accordance with professional standards and the employer's instructions, provided such instructions do not conflict with the contract, the law, or public morals and do not expose the worker to danger.
2. Exercise due care in respect of machinery, tools, equipment, and raw materials belonging to the employer that are placed at the worker's disposal or entrusted to the worker, and return to the employer any unused materials.
3. Observe proper conduct and morals during work.
4. Provide all necessary assistance, without requiring additional pay, in cases of disasters and dangers threatening the safety of the workplace or persons working therein.
5. Submit, at the employer's request, to medical examinations that the employer wishes to conduct before or during employment in order to verify that the worker is free from occupational or communicable diseases.
6. Preserve technical, commercial, and industrial secrets relating to materials produced by the worker or to whose production the worker directly or indirectly contributes, and all professional secrets relating to the work or establishment whose disclosure could harm the employer's interests.
original_text:
In addition to the duties prescribed by this Law and by the regulations and decisions issued for its implementation, a worker shall:
1. Perform the work in accordance with professional standards and the employer's instructions, provided such instructions do not conflict with the contract, the law, or public morals and do not expose the worker to danger.
2. Exercise due care in respect of machinery, tools, equipment, and raw materials belonging to the employer that are placed at the worker's disposal or entrusted to the worker, and return to the employer any unused materials.
3. Observe proper conduct and morals during work.
4. Provide all necessary assistance, without requiring additional pay, in cases of disasters and dangers threatening the safety of the workplace or persons working therein.
5. Submit, at the employer's request, to medical examinations that the employer wishes to conduct before or during employment in order to verify that the worker is free from occupational or communicable diseases.
6. Preserve technical, commercial, and industrial secrets relating to materials produced by the worker or to whose production the worker directly or indirectly contributes, and all professional secrets relating to the work or establishment whose disclosure could harm the employer's interests.

description:
The disciplinary penalties that an employer may impose on a worker are:
1. Warning.
2. Fine.
3. Deprivation of, or postponement of, an increment for a period not exceeding one year, where such increment is provided by the employer.
4. Postponement of promotion for a period not exceeding one year, where promotion is provided by the employer.
5. Suspension from work without pay.
6. Dismissal in the cases prescribed by law.
original_text:
The disciplinary penalties that an employer may impose on a worker are:
1. Warning.
2. Fine.
3. Deprivation of, or postponement of, an increment for a period not exceeding one year, where such increment is provided by the employer.
4. Postponement of promotion for a period not exceeding one year, where promotion is provided by the employer.
5. Suspension from work without pay.
6. Dismissal in the cases prescribed by law.

description: An employer may not impose a penalty not provided for in this Law or in the work organization regulations.
original_text: An employer may not impose on a worker a penalty that is not provided for in this Law or in the work organization regulations.

rule_name: Penalty Not Increased for Repeated Violations
description: A penalty may not be increased on account of a repeated violation if one hundred and eighty days have elapsed since the worker was notified of the penalty imposed for the previous violation.
condition: one hundred and eighty days have elapsed
original_text: A penalty may not be increased on account of a repeated violation if one hundred and eighty days have elapsed since the worker was notified of the penalty imposed for the previous violation.

description: A worker may not be accused of a violation more than thirty days after its discovery.
original_text: A worker may not be accused of a violation more than thirty days after its discovery.

rule_name: Disciplinary Penalty Not Imposed for Acts Outside Workplace
description: A disciplinary penalty may not be imposed for an act committed by the worker outside the workplace unless the act is connected with the work, the employer, or the responsible manager.
original_text: A disciplinary penalty may not be imposed for an act committed by the worker outside the workplace unless the act is connected with the work, the employer, or the responsible manager.

rule_name: Disciplinary Penalty Not Imposed for Minor Violations
description: For a single violation, the worker may not be fined more than the equivalent of five days' wages, may not be subjected to more than one penalty, may not have more than five days' wages deducted in any one month in satisfaction of fines, and may not be suspended without pay for more than five days in any one month.
original_text: A disciplinary penalty may not be imposed for a single violation, the worker may not be fined more than the equivalent of five days' wages, may not be subjected to more than one penalty, may not have more than five days' wages deducted in any one month in satisfaction of fines, and may not be suspended without pay for more than five days in any one month.

description: The worker shall be notified in writing of the decision imposing a penalty. If the worker refuses to receive the notice or is absent, it shall be sent by registered mail to the address recorded in the worker's file.
original_text: The worker shall be notified in writing of the decision imposing a penalty. If the worker refuses to receive the notice or is absent, it shall be sent by registered mail to the address recorded in the worker's file.

description: The worker may submit a written grievance to the competent authority within the employer's organization within thirty days, excluding official holidays, from the date of notification.
original_text: The worker may submit a written grievance to the competent authority within the employer's organization within thirty days, excluding official holidays, from the date of notification.

description: An employer shall record fines imposed on workers in a special register stating the worker's name, wage, amount of the fine, reason for imposing it, and date thereof. Fines may be used only for purposes benefiting the workers of the establishment.
original_text: An employer shall record fines imposed on workers in a special register stating the worker's name, wage, amount of the fine, reason for imposing it, and date thereof. Fines may be used only for purposes benefiting the workers of the establishment.

rule_name: Termination of the activity in which the worker is employed, unless otherwise agreed
description: Termination of the activity in which the worker is employed, unless otherwise agreed.
original_text: Termination of the activity in which the worker is employed, unless otherwise agreed.

description: A resignation request is deemed accepted if 30 days pass without a response from the employer. The employer may postpone acceptance for up to 60 days with a written, reasoned explanation.
original_text: A resignation request shall be deemed accepted if thirty days pass from the date of submission without a response from the employer. Where required in the interests of work, the employer may postpone acceptance of the resignation for a period not exceeding sixty days by providing the worker with a written, reasoned explanation before the expiry of the thirty-day period referred to in this paragraph. The postponement period shall be calculated from the date on which the explanation is provided to the worker.

description: The employment contract terminates by resignation on the date the employer accepts the resignation, upon expiry of the 30-day period without a response, or upon expiry of the postponement period.
original_text: The employment contract shall terminate by resignation on the date the employer accepts the resignation, upon expiry of the thirty-day period referred to in paragraph (1) without a response from the employer, or upon expiry of the postponement period referred to in paragraph (1), as applicable.

description: A worker may withdraw the resignation request within a period not exceeding 7 days from the date of submission, unless the employer accepts it before the withdrawal.
original_text: The worker may withdraw the resignation request within a period not exceeding seven days from the date of submission, unless the employer accepts it before the withdrawal.

description: A resignation request may not specify a deferred future effective date.
original_text: A resignation request may not specify a deferred future effective date.

description: The employment contract remains in force during the period in which the resignation request is pending, and both parties continue to perform all obligations arising from it.
original_text: The employment contract shall remain in force during the period in which the resignation request is pending, and both parties shall continue to perform all obligations arising from it.

description: A worker whose contract terminates by resignation is entitled to all rights granted under this Law.
original_text: A worker whose contract terminates by resignation shall be entitled to all rights granted under this Law.

description: If the employer, a member of the employer's family, or the responsible manager commits an assault involving violence or engages in indecent conduct toward the worker or a member of the worker's family.
original_text: If the employer, a member of the employer's family, or the responsible manager commits an assault involving violence or engages in indecent conduct toward the worker or a member of the worker's family.

description: If the employer or responsible manager treats the worker with cruelty, injustice, or humiliation.
original_text: If the employer or responsible manager treats the worker with cruelty, injustice, or humiliation.

rule_name: Serious Danger to Safety or Health
description: If a serious danger at the workplace threatens the worker's safety or health, provided the employer is aware of the danger and fails to take measures indicating its removal.
original_text: If a serious danger at the workplace threatens the worker's safety or health, provided the employer is aware of the danger and fails to take measures indicating its removal.

description: The employer shall settle all of the worker's rights within a period not exceeding two weeks.
original_text: terminates the contract, the employer shall settle all of the worker's rights within a period not exceeding two weeks. The employer may deduct from amounts due to the worker any debt owed to the employer by reason of the work.

description: The Council of Ministers may establish a minimum wage upon a proposal from the Minister.
original_text: Where necessary, and upon a proposal from the Minister, the Council of Ministers may establish a minimum wage.

description: Wages must be paid in the official currency of the Kingdom and in accordance with specific rules.
applicability: Daily-paid workers, Monthly-paid workers, Piece-rate workers, Other workers
original_text: A worker's wage and all other amounts due to the worker shall be paid in the official currency of the Kingdom in accordance with the following rules:

description: Establishments must deposit wages into workers' accounts through approved banks by the payment dates.
original_text: Establishments shall deposit wages into workers' accounts through banks approved in the Kingdom no later than the payment dates prescribed above. The Minister may exempt certain establishments from this requirement.

description: The employer may deduct from the worker's wage the amount necessary to repair damage caused by the worker, not exceeding five days' wages in any one month.
applicability: Worker causing damage to machinery or products
original_text: If a worker, through fault or violation of the employer's instructions, causes the loss of, damage to, or destruction of machinery or products owned by or entrusted to the employer, and such loss or damage is not caused by a third party or by force majeure, the employer may deduct from the worker's wage the amount necessary to repair the damage or restore the situation to its former condition. The amount deducted for this purpose shall not exceed five days' wages in any one month.

description: A grievance by either party must be submitted within fifteen working days, otherwise the right to grieve lapses.
original_text: A grievance by either party shall be submitted within fifteen working days, failing which the right to grieve shall lapse.

description: Private rights can be deducted from the worker's wage with the worker's written consent, except in specific cases.
original_text: No amount may be deducted from a worker's wage in respect of private rights without the worker's written consent, except in the following cases:

description: Working hours and rest periods shall be arranged so that a worker does not work for more than five consecutive hours without a period of at least thirty minutes at a time for rest, prayer, and meals during the total working hours, and so that the worker does not remain at the workplace for more than twelve hours in any one day.
original_text: Working hours and rest periods shall be arranged so that a worker does not work for more than five consecutive hours without a period of at least thirty minutes at a time for rest, prayer, and meals during the total working hours, and so that the worker does not remain at the workplace for more than twelve hours in any one day.

description: Periods designated for rest, prayer, and meals shall not be included in actual working hours. During such periods the worker shall not be under the employer's authority, and the employer may not require the worker to remain at the workplace.
original_text: Periods designated for rest, prayer, and meals shall not be included in actual working hours. During such periods the worker shall not be under the employer's authority, and the employer may not require the worker to remain at the workplace.

description: The employer shall pay the worker for overtime an additional amount equal to the hourly wage plus 50% of the worker's basic hourly wage. With the worker's consent, the employer may instead grant paid compensatory leave in lieu of the overtime pay due to the worker.
original_text: The employer shall pay the worker for overtime an additional amount equal to the hourly wage plus 50% of the worker's basic hourly wage. With the worker's consent, the employer may instead grant paid compensatory leave in lieu of the overtime pay due to the worker. The Implementing Regulations shall specify the provisions relating thereto.

description: Hours exceeding the hours adopted for the weekly standard for working hours shall be regarded as overtime.
original_text: Where an establishment applies the weekly standard for working hours, hours exceeding the hours adopted for that standard shall be regarded as overtime.

description: All hours worked on holidays and official feast days shall be regarded as overtime.
original_text: All hours worked on holidays and official feast days shall be regarded as overtime.

description: A worker is entitled to paid leave of not less than ten days and not more than fifteen days, including the Eid al-Adha holiday, to perform the Hajj pilgrimage once during the worker's service, provided the worker has not previously performed Hajj.
original_text: A worker shall be entitled to paid leave of not less than ten days and not more than fifteen days, including the Eid al-Adha holiday, to perform the Hajj pilgrimage once during the worker's service, provided the worker has not previously performed Hajj.

description: If the employer approves a worker's enrollment in, or continuation at, an educational institution, the worker shall be entitled to fully paid leave to sit examinations for a non-repeated academic year, for the actual number of examination days. If the examination relates to a repeated academic year, the worker shall be entitled to unpaid leave for the actual number of examination days. The worker shall be deprived of the leave pay if it is established that the worker did not sit the examination, without prejudice to the employer's right to take disciplinary action.
original_text: 1. If the employer approves a worker's enrollment in, or continuation at, an educational institution, the worker shall be entitled to fully paid leave to sit examinations for a non-repeated academic year, for the actual number of examination days. If the examination relates to a repeated academic year, the worker shall be entitled to unpaid leave for the actual number of examination days. The worker shall be deprived of the leave pay if it is established that the worker did not sit the examination, without prejudice to the employer's right to take disciplinary action.

description: If the worker has not obtained the employer's approval for enrollment in an educational institution, the worker may take leave for the actual number of examination days from annual leave, if available. If annual leave is unavailable, the worker may take unpaid leave for the actual number of examination days.
original_text: 2. If the worker has not obtained the employer's approval for enrollment in an educational institution, the worker may take leave for the actual number of examination days from annual leave, if available. If annual leave is unavailable, the worker may take unpaid leave for the actual number of examination days.

description: The worker shall apply for such leave at least fifteen days before it begins.
original_text: The worker shall apply for such leave at least fifteen days before it begins.

description: The employer may require documents supporting the leave request and proof that the worker sat the examination.
original_text: The employer may require documents supporting the leave request and proof that the worker sat the examination.

description: A worker whose illness is established shall be entitled, during a single year, to sick leave with full pay for the first thirty days, three-quarters pay for the following sixty days, and without pay for the following thirty days, whether such leave is continuous or intermittent. For the purposes of this Article, the year shall begin on the date of the first sick leave.
original_text: A worker whose illness is established shall be entitled, during a single year, to sick leave with full pay for the first thirty days, three-quarters pay for the following sixty days, and without pay for the following thirty days, whether such leave is continuous or intermittent. For the purposes of this Article, the year shall begin on the date of the first sick leave.

rule_name: Unpaid Leave for Leave Exceeding 20 Days
description: While taking any leave provided for in this Chapter, a worker may not work for another employer. If the employer establishes that the worker has done so, the employer may withhold the worker's wage for the period of leave or recover any leave pay already paid for that period.
original_text: While taking any leave provided for in this Chapter, a worker may not work for another employer. If the employer establishes that the worker has done so, the employer may withhold the worker's wage for the period of leave or recover any leave pay already paid for that period.

rule_name: Full-time workers not considered part-time due to reduction in normal working hours
description: Full-time workers affected by a collective and temporary reduction in their normal working hours for economic, technical, or structural reasons shall not be regarded as part-time workers.
applicability: Applicable to full-time workers affected by a collective and temporary reduction in their normal working hours for economic, technical, or structural reasons.
original_text: Full-time workers who are affected by a collective and temporary reduction in their normal working hours for economic, technical, or structural reasons shall not be regarded as part-time workers.

rule_name: Regulation of part-time work by the Minister
description: The Minister shall issue the rules and controls necessary to regulate part-time work, specifying the obligations of both the part-time worker and the employer.
applicability: Applicable to the regulations issued by the Minister regarding part-time work.
original_text: The Minister shall issue the rules and controls necessary to regulate part-time work, specifying the obligations of both the part-time worker and the employer. The provisions of this Law shall apply only to the extent determined by the Minister, except for the protections afforded to comparable full-time workers in respect of occupational safety and health and work injuries.

description: The employer shall maintain the establishment in a sanitary and clean condition, provide adequate lighting and water suitable for drinking and washing, and comply with occupational protection, safety, and health rules, procedures, and standards prescribed by the Minister.
original_text: The employer shall maintain the establishment in a sanitary and clean condition, provide adequate lighting and water suitable for drinking and washing, and comply with such other occupational protection, safety, and health rules, procedures, and standards as may be prescribed by decision of the Minister.

description: Every employer shall take the necessary precautions to protect workers against hazards, occupational diseases, and machinery used in the workplace, and ensure occupational protection and safety.
original_text: Every employer shall take the necessary precautions to protect workers against hazards, occupational diseases, and machinery used in the workplace, and ensure occupational protection and safety.

description: The employer shall post instructions concerning the safety of work and workers in a conspicuous place in the establishment, in Arabic and, where necessary, in any other language understood by the workers.
original_text: The employer shall post, in a conspicuous place in the establishment, instructions concerning the safety of work and workers, in Arabic and, where necessary, in any other language understood by the workers.

description: Before a worker commences work, the employer shall inform the worker of the occupational hazards associated with the work and shall require the worker to use the prescribed protective measures.
original_text: Before a worker commences work, the employer shall inform the worker of the occupational hazards associated with the work and shall require the worker to use the prescribed protective measures.

description: The employer shall provide workers with suitable personal protective equipment and train them in its use.
original_text: The employer shall provide workers with suitable personal protective equipment and train them in its use.

description: A worker shall use the protective equipment assigned to each operation, preserve such equipment, and comply with the instructions established to safeguard the worker's health and protect the worker against injuries and diseases.
original_text: A worker shall use the protective equipment assigned to each operation, preserve such equipment, and comply with the instructions established to safeguard the worker's health and protect the worker against injuries and diseases.

rule_name: Preventing Fires and Providing Firefighting Equipment
description: The employer shall take the necessary precautions to prevent fires and provide the technical means required for firefighting, including escape exits that remain usable at all times. Detailed instructions concerning fire-prevention measures shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the workplace.
original_text: The employer shall take the necessary precautions to prevent fires and provide the technical means required for firefighting, including escape exits that remain usable at all times. Detailed instructions concerning fire-prevention measures shall be posted in a conspicuous place at the workplace.

description: The employer shall be responsible for emergencies and accidents suffered by persons other than the employer's workers who enter the workplace by virtue of their duties or with the approval of the employer or the employer's agents, where such emergencies or accidents result from a failure to take the technical precautions required by the nature of the work.
original_text: The employer shall be responsible for emergencies and accidents suffered by persons other than the employer's workers who enter the workplace by virtue of their duties or with the approval of the employer or the employer's agents, where such emergencies or accidents result from a failure to take the technical precautions required by the nature of the work.

description: A sudden occurrence, such as a major release, fire, or explosion, arising in the course of an activity within a major-hazard establishment, involving one or more hazardous substances, and resulting in a serious danger to workers, the public, or the environment, whether immediate or delayed.
original_text: Major accident means any sudden occurrence, such as a major release, fire, or explosion, arising in the course of an activity within a major-hazard establishment, involving one or more hazardous substances, and resulting in a serious danger to workers, the public, or the environment, whether immediate or delayed.

description: The Ministry shall establish criteria for identifying major-hazard establishments on the basis of a list of hazardous substances, categories of such substances, or both.
original_text: The Ministry shall establish criteria for identifying major-hazard establishments on the basis of a list of hazardous substances, categories of such substances, or both.

rule_name: Determination of status and classification of establishments
description: Employers shall, in coordination with the Ministry, determine the status and classification of their establishments on the basis of the criteria referred to in Article 129 of this Law.
original_text: Employers shall, in coordination with the Ministry, determine the status and classification of their establishments on the basis of the criteria referred to in Article 129 of this Law.

rule_name: Regulations and decisions for major-hazard establishments
description: The Minister shall issue regulations and decisions setting out the arrangements required at the establishment level for the prevention of major hazards, the duties of employers in this regard, the arrangements to protect the public and the environment outside the site of each major-hazard establishment, the rights and duties of workers, and any other measures necessary to prevent major accidents, reduce the likelihood of their occurrence, and limit their effects.
original_text: The Minister shall issue regulations and decisions setting out the arrangements required at the establishment level for the prevention of major hazards, the duties of employers in this regard, the arrangements to protect the public and the environment outside the site of each major-hazard establishment, the rights and duties of workers, and any other measures necessary to prevent major accidents, reduce the likelihood of their occurrence, and limit their effects.

rule_name: Identification of hazardous occupations and work
description: The Minister shall, by decision, identify occupations and work that are considered hazardous or harmful, or that may expose workers to unusual risks or harm, as well as the categories of persons whose employment in such occupations or work is permanently or temporarily prohibited or is subject to special conditions. This may include determining whether working times should be restricted for any such category, in a manner consistent with the Kingdom's relevant obligations under international conventions.
original_text: The Minister shall, by decision, identify occupations and work that are considered hazardous or harmful, or that may expose workers to unusual risks or harm, as well as the categories of persons whose employment in such occupations or work is permanently or temporarily prohibited or is subject to special conditions. This may include determining whether working times should be restricted for any such category, in a manner consistent with the Kingdom's relevant obligations under international conventions.

description: If a worker is unable to work due to injury, the employment contract shall terminate, and the worker shall be compensated for the injury.
original_text: If a worker is unable to work due to injury, the injury shall be regarded as a total disability, the employment contract shall terminate, and the worker shall be compensated for the injury.

rule_name: Compensation for Total Permanent Disability or Death
description: If a work injury results in total permanent disability or death, the injured worker or the worker's beneficiaries shall be entitled to compensation equal to three years' wages, provided that the amount shall not be less than SAR 54,000.
original_text: If a work injury results in total permanent disability or death, the injured worker or the worker's beneficiaries shall be entitled to compensation equal to three years' wages, provided that the amount shall not be less than SAR 54,000.

rule_name: Liability of Former Employers for Occupational Diseases
description: The liability of former employers for whom a worker previously worked shall be determined in light of the medical report of the treating physician. Such employers shall be required to pay the compensation provided for in Article 138 of this Law, each in proportion to the period during which the injured worker was employed by that employer.
original_text: The liability of former employers for whom a worker previously worked shall be determined in light of the medical report of the treating physician. Such employers shall be required to pay the compensation provided for in Article 138 of this Law, each in proportion to the period during which the injured worker was employed by that employer.

description: The procedures for reporting work injuries shall be determined by decision of the Minister.
original_text: The procedures for reporting work injuries shall be determined by decision of the Minister.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Essential Necessities
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide shops selling food, clothing, and other essential necessities at reasonable prices in work areas where such shops are not ordinarily available.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
1. Shops selling food, clothing, and other essential necessities at reasonable prices in work areas where such shops are not ordinarily available.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Recreational and Educational Facilities
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide suitable recreational and educational facilities and sports grounds attached to workplaces.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
2. Suitable recreational and educational facilities and sports grounds attached to workplaces.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Medical Arrangements
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide appropriate medical arrangements necessary to preserve workers' health and to provide comprehensive treatment for their families. For this purpose, 'family' means the spouse, children, mother, and father residing with the worker.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
3. Appropriate medical arrangements necessary to preserve workers' health and to provide comprehensive treatment for their families. For this purpose, 'family' means the spouse, children, mother, and father residing with the worker.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Schools for Workers' Children
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide schools for workers' children where sufficient schools are not available in the area.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
4. Schools for workers' children where sufficient schools are not available in the area.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Mosques or Prayer Areas
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide mosques or prayer areas at workplaces.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
6. Mosques or prayer areas at workplaces.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Literacy Programs
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide literacy programs for workers.
applicability: Workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text:
With respect to workers performing work in locations remote from populated areas, the employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide all or some of the following, as determined by the Minister:
5. Literacy programs for workers.

rule_name: Employer Obligation to Provide Housing and Meals
description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide housing, camps, and meals for the workers.
applicability: Employers whose workers perform work in locations remote from populated areas, mines, and quarries, or at oil-exploration centers
original_text:
An employer whose workers perform work in locations remote from populated areas, in mines and quarries, or at oil-exploration centers shall provide housing, camps, and meals for the workers.
The Minister shall, by decision, determine the conditions and specifications for housing and camps, the charge for use of housing, the number of meals, quantities and types of food and the conditions applicable thereto, the amount to be borne by the worker for meals, and any other requirements necessary to preserve workers' health.

description: The employer shall, at the employer's expense, provide transportation from the workers' places of residence, or from a designated assembly point, to the workplaces and back each day where those workplaces are not served by regular transportation operating at times compatible with working hours.
applicability: Employers whose workers perform work in locations remote from populated areas
original_text: Every employer shall provide workers with transportation from their places of residence, or from a designated assembly point, to the workplaces and back each day where those workplaces are not served by regular transportation operating at times compatible with working hours.

description: A female worker shall be entitled to maternity leave with full pay for a period of twelve weeks. The six weeks following childbirth shall be compulsory leave, and the worker may distribute the remaining six weeks as she sees fit, beginning from four weeks before the expected date of delivery.
original_text: 1. A female worker shall be entitled to maternity leave with full pay for a period of twelve weeks. The six weeks following childbirth shall be compulsory leave, and the worker may distribute the remaining six weeks as she sees fit, beginning from four weeks before the expected date of delivery. The expected date of delivery shall be established by a medical certificate certified by a health authority. If, because childbirth occurs later than expected, the remaining leave is less than six weeks, the period required to complete the six weeks shall be treated as unpaid leave. In all cases, the female worker may extend this leave for one additional month without pay.

rule_name: Additional Fully Paid Leave for Sick Child or Child with Disability
description: If a female worker gives birth to a sick child or a child with a disability whose health condition requires a continuous companion, she shall be entitled to one month of fully paid leave beginning after the end of maternity leave. She may extend that leave for one additional month without pay.
applicability: Female workers who give birth to a sick child or a child with a disability whose health condition requires a continuous companion
original_text: 2. If a female worker gives birth to a sick child or a child with a disability whose health condition requires a continuous companion, she shall be entitled to one month of fully paid leave beginning after the end of maternity leave. She may extend that leave for one additional month without pay.

rule_name: Medical Care During Pregnancy and Childbirth
description: The employer shall provide medical care to a female worker during pregnancy and childbirth.
original_text: Article 153. The employer shall provide medical care to a female worker during pregnancy and childbirth.

description: When a female worker returns to work after maternity leave, she shall be entitled, for the purpose of nursing her child, to one or more rest periods whose total duration does not exceed one hour per day, in addition to the rest periods granted to all workers. Such period or periods shall be counted as actual working hours and shall not result in any reduction in wage.
original_text: Article 154. When a female worker returns to work after maternity leave, she shall be entitled, for the purpose of nursing her child, to one or more rest periods whose total duration does not exceed one hour per day, in addition to the rest periods granted to all workers. Such period or periods shall be counted as actual working hours and shall not result in any reduction in wage.

rule_name: Protection from Dismissal During Pregnancy and Maternity Leave
description: An employer may not dismiss a female worker, or give her notice of dismissal, during her pregnancy or while she is on maternity leave. This protection shall also cover illness arising from either pregnancy or childbirth, provided that the illness is established by an approved medical certificate and that the total period of absence does not exceed one hundred and eighty days in a year, whether continuous or intermittent.
original_text: Article 155. An employer may not dismiss a female worker, or give her notice of dismissal, during her pregnancy or while she is on maternity leave. This protection shall also cover illness arising from either pregnancy or childbirth, provided that the illness is established by an approved medical certificate and that the total period of absence does not exceed one hundred and eighty days in a year, whether continuous or intermittent.

rule_name: Forfeiture of Entitlements During Authorized Leave
description: A female worker shall forfeit the entitlements granted under this Part if she works for another employer during her authorized leave. In such a case, the original employer may withhold her wage for the period of leave or recover any amount already paid to her for that period.
original_text: Article 157. A female worker shall forfeit the entitlements granted under this Part if she works for another employer during her authorized leave. In such a case, the original employer may withhold her wage for the period of leave or recover any amount already paid to her for that period.

description: At every workplace where women are employed, and in all occupations, the employer shall provide seats for female workers so that they may rest.
applicability: Every workplace where women are employed, and in all occupations.
original_text: At every workplace where women are employed, and in all occupations, the employer shall provide seats for female workers so that they may rest.

description: Every employer employing fifty or more female workers shall provide a suitable place with a sufficient number of caregivers to care for the children of female workers who are under six years of age, where the number of such children is ten or more.
applicability: Every employer employing fifty or more female workers.
original_text: Every employer employing fifty or more female workers shall provide a suitable place with a sufficient number of caregivers to care for the children of female workers who are under six years of age, where the number of such children is ten or more.

description: The Minister may require an employer employing one hundred or more female workers in a single city to establish a nursery independently or jointly with other employers in the same city, or to contract with an existing nursery, to care for the children of female workers who are under six years of age during working hours. In such a case, the Minister shall determine the conditions and arrangements governing the nursery and the proportion of costs to be borne by the female workers benefiting from the service.
condition: one hundred or more female workers in a single city
applicability: The Minister may require an employer employing one hundred or more female workers in a single city.
original_text: The Minister may require an employer employing one hundred or more female workers in a single city to establish a nursery independently or jointly with other employers in the same city, or to contract with an existing nursery, to care for the children of female workers who are under six years of age during working hours. In such a case, the Minister shall determine the conditions and arrangements governing the nursery and the proportion of costs to be borne by the female workers benefiting from the service.

rule_name: Payment of amounts to seafarer in official currency
description: All amounts due to a seafarer shall be paid in the official currency. They may be paid in a foreign currency where they fall due while the ship is outside territorial waters and the seafarer agrees to such payment.
original_text: All amounts due to a seafarer shall be paid in the official currency. They may be paid in a foreign currency where they fall due while the ship is outside territorial waters and the seafarer agrees to such payment.

rule_name: Wage not reduced for shortened voyage
description: If a voyage is shortened for any reason, whether voluntarily or by force majeure, the wage of a seafarer employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage shall not be reduced as a result.
applicability: Seafarers employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage
original_text: If a voyage is shortened for any reason, whether voluntarily or by force majeure, the wage of a seafarer employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage shall not be reduced as a result.

rule_name: Seafarer's wage not entitled to compensation for cancelled voyage
description: The seafarer shall not be entitled to compensation if the voyage is cancelled, nor to an increase in wage if the voyage is delayed or prolonged.
applicability: Seafarer employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage
original_text: The seafarer shall not be entitled to compensation if the voyage is cancelled, nor to an increase in wage if the voyage is delayed or prolonged.

rule_name: Seafarer's wage entitled to compensation for delay or prolongation
description: However, if the delay or prolongation results from an act of the shippers, the seafarer shall be entitled to compensation from the shipowner/operator.
applicability: Seafarer employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage
original_text: However, if the delay or prolongation results from an act of the shippers, the seafarer shall be entitled to compensation from the shipowner/operator.

rule_name: Wage up to date of incident for ship captured, sunk, or unseaworthy
description: If the ship is captured, sinks, or becomes unseaworthy, the seafarer shall be entitled to wages up to the date on which the incident occurs.
applicability: Seafarer employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage
original_text: If the ship is captured, sinks, or becomes unseaworthy, the seafarer shall be entitled to wages up to the date on which the incident occurs.

rule_name: Working hours aboard ship not exceed 14 hours in 24-hour period
description: Working hours aboard a ship while it is at sea shall not exceed fourteen hours in any twenty-four-hour period or seventy-two hours in any seven-day period.
original_text: Working hours aboard a ship while it is at sea shall not exceed fourteen hours in any twenty-four-hour period or seventy-two hours in any seven-day period.

rule_name: Seafarer entitled to share of reward for assisting or rescuing another ship
description: Every seafarer who contributes to assisting or rescuing another ship shall be entitled to a share of the reward earned by the ship on which the seafarer works, regardless of the form of remuneration received for the work performed.
original_text: Every seafarer who contributes to assisting or rescuing another ship shall be entitled to a share of the reward earned by the ship on which the seafarer works, regardless of the form of remuneration received for the work performed.

rule_name: Seafarer's heirs entitled to wage up to date of death
description: If a seafarer dies during a voyage, the seafarer's heirs shall be entitled to the wage due up to the date of death where the wage is calculated monthly. If the wage is calculated by voyage, the heirs shall be entitled to the wage for the entire voyage. If the wage consists of a share of profits, the full share shall become due.
original_text: If a seafarer dies during a voyage, the seafarer's heirs shall be entitled to the wage due up to the date of death where the wage is calculated monthly. If the wage is calculated by voyage, the heirs shall be entitled to the wage for the entire voyage. If the wage consists of a share of profits, the full share shall become due.

rule_name: Employer may terminate contract without prior notice and without compensation
description: The employer may terminate the contract without prior notice and without compensation if the voyage is cancelled before it begins for a reason beyond the control of the shipowner/operator and the wage is based on a single voyage, unless the contract provides otherwise.
applicability: Seafarers employed under a maritime employment contract for a single voyage
original_text: The employer may terminate the contract without prior notice and without compensation if the voyage is cancelled before it begins for a reason beyond the control of the shipowner/operator and the wage is based on a single voyage, unless the contract provides otherwise.

description: The shipowner/operator shall repatriate the seafarer to the seafarer's home country in the following cases:
applicability: Applicable to seafarers in the following cases:
original_text:
The shipowner/operator shall repatriate the seafarer to the seafarer's home country in the following cases:
1. If the voyage is cancelled by the act of the shipowner/operator after the ship has departed.
2. If the voyage is cancelled after the ship has sailed because trade with the destination designated for the voyage has been prohibited.
3. If the seafarer is removed from the ship because of illness, injury, or disability.
4. If the ship is sold in a foreign country.
5. If the seafarer is dismissed from service during the voyage without lawful justification.
6. If the contract concluded with the seafarer expires at a port other than the port specified in the contract.

description: No person under eighteen years of age may be employed in a mine or quarry.
applicability: Applicable to all mines and quarries
original_text: No person under eighteen years of age may be employed in a mine or quarry.

rule_name: Medical examination requirement for work in mines and quarries
description: No person may be permitted to work in operations to which this Part applies unless the person has undergone a comprehensive medical examination and has been found medically fit for the required work.
applicability: Applicable to all mines and quarries
original_text: No person may be permitted to work in operations to which this Part applies unless the person has undergone a comprehensive medical examination and has been found medically fit for the required work.

description: Such examination shall be repeated periodically, and the worker may not be charged any expense for the required medical examinations.
applicability: Applicable to all mines and quarries
original_text: Such examination shall be repeated periodically, and the worker may not be charged any expense for the required medical examinations.

description: The employer shall establish a rescue station close to the workplace, equipped with the necessary rescue and first-aid equipment.
applicability: Applicable to all mines and quarries
